title: Platform operator — wire shapes, version 1
description: The machine-readable half of platform-operator-v1.contract.yaml. BOTH ARE NORMATIVE TOGETHER. Nothing in this repository executes JSON Schema: there is no implementation, no package.json and no node_modules, so this file is normative and hand-checked, never machine-validated. No report may describe it as validated.

organizationId.description: An opaque, non-sequential, unguessable identifier. 128 bits of base64url as generated (kernel/ids.ts), 22 characters; the bound is wider than the generator so a longer historical value is not rejected. It is NEVER parsed, decoded or interpreted by a client.

principalId.description: Same shape and same rules as organizationId. A separate definition rather than a $ref to it, deliberately: the two are different KINDS of identifier that happen to share a grammar, and one $def would let a future widening of one silently widen the other.

organizationStatus.description:
As stored in the control plane's organization table. An unrecognised STORED value is never rendered to a client, because Core validates on read and treats an unknown value as unavailable rather than passing it through.

*** THIS DESCRIPTION SAID 'A CLOSED SET' AND THAT SENTENCE ANSWERS A DIFFERENT QUESTION FROM THE ONE `enumPolicy` ASKS. *** Corrected 2026-09-09. Core refusing to render a CORRUPT stored value is protection against schema drift; it says nothing about whether a NEW value may be added legitimately. Those are two questions and the word 'closed' answers only the first. When a third state ships — suspension already has a named future route, and `core.platform-organization.update` explicitly 'DOES NOT COVER STATUS' — Core's union widens and it emits the new value correctly, at which point a client holding a closed union has a wrong type. See `enumPolicy`.

DUPLICATED: `organization-detail-v1`'s `organizationSummary.status` carries the same two values for the same wire field. Both are declared `extensible` and MUST stay agreed; see that file.

platformRole.description:
The union stored in platform_operator.platform_role, mirroring permission-catalog.yaml's platform-scope seed roles. An unrecognised stored value denies everything and never reaches a response.

`extensible`, AND THE CATALOGUE ITSELF IS THE ARGUMENT: it already anticipates a third role — 'a break-glass responder role can hold REVOKE without GRANT, so the person reachable at 3am can cut off a compromised operator without themselves being able to create one' — and records that the permission making that a catalogue edit rather than a redesign already exists. A client that breaks when that role appears would make adding it a client release.

DUPLICATED THREE WAYS, and this is the one to watch: `platform-operators-v1` and `platform-audit-read-v1` each define `platformRole` with the same two values. All three must carry the same policy, and nothing checks that they do.

permissionId.description: A registered permission identifier. The pattern is permission-catalog.yaml's namePattern, restated rather than $ref-ed because that file is YAML and this is JSON — a divergence between them is a defect qa-agent should catch, and the catalog is the authority.

cursor.description: An opaque pagination cursor. Never constructed, parsed or modified by a client. Null means there is no further page. CORRECTED 2026-09-05: this previously read 'opaque, TENANT-BOUND pagination cursor', copied from the Action-class contracts where it is correct. A PLATFORM ROUTE HAS NO TENANT (platform-operator-v1 P1), so there is nothing to bind to and TenantBoundCursorCodec is not reachable from this class. `core-agent` built a separate tenant-free codec and reported the mismatch rather than binding a cursor to a tenant that does not exist — which is the right call and the reason this is a two-line correction instead of a defect. THE CURSOR IS BOUND TO THE PRINCIPAL AND THE QUERY SHAPE INSTEAD: it must not be transferable between operators, or one operator could resume another's enumeration of the platform's Organizations.

organizationSummary.description:
One row of the platform's Organization list.

CORRECTED 2026-09-07. IT SAID 'there is no name, because control-plane/0002_organization.sql declined a name column and the organization-structure slice owns it.' THAT SENTENCE IS NOW FALSE AND IT IS THE KIND THAT STOPS A READER LOOKING — organization-identity-v1 and docs/decisions/0031 own `display_name`, and it is in this shape. The name is null until the column lands; what changed is that there is a contract for it and a route that sets it.

NOTE WHAT IS STILL ABSENT AND WHY, because that half is unchanged: THERE IS NO COUNT OF ANYTHING — no customers, no members, no activity, no usage. Every one of those would be a read behind whereWithTenant, and a console acquires cross-tenant reach one convenient number at a time.

AND THE REGISTRATIONS ARE DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. `commercial_registration` and `vat_registration` are on the DETAIL response only: two objects per row inflate every page of a listing that needs a label, and the detail route is one click away. Adding them later is additive.

display_name.description:
THE ORGANIZATION'S NAME. Canonical definition: urn:dudo:schema:organization-identity:1#/$defs/displayName, restated rather than $ref'd because no URN resolver exists (AS1); the 200 bound is the one this field already published.

*** MOVED INTO `required` ON 2026-09-07, AND THAT IS A DEFECT FIX RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. *** It was in `properties` and not in `required`, so under `additionalProperties: false` it was A PERMITTED OPTIONAL FIELD — while this description said it was present so that names would be additive, and the identical field in organization-detail-v1 was required-and-nullable. THE PROSE AND THE MACHINE-READABLE HALF DISAGREED ABOUT THE SAME FIELD IN TWO CONTRACTS, which is workflow.md §12 in its purest form: prose describes, `required` instructs. It was latent only because the value was always null, and it stopped being latent the moment a client began depending on the field being there.

Null until control-plane/0002_organization.sql carries the column and an operator sets a value. A client renders organization_id verbatim when this is null and must not substitute a placeholder of its own.

organizationCountOutput.description: How many Organizations exist on the platform. The number `platform.organizations.list` cannot state, because a paginated list can only say 'at least 25' until its last page.

total.description: The number of rows in the control-plane `organization` table. ZERO IS A VALID, REACHABLE ANSWER and is not an error or an empty state — a platform with no Organizations yet is the ordinary first day. IT MUST BE A COUNT AND NEVER A FETCH-AND-LENGTH: reading every row to measure the length is the same number on the wire and a different number against d1-rows-read.

organizationCountOutput.$comment:
*** A SCALAR AND NOTHING ELSE. `additionalProperties: false` IS THE ENFORCEMENT OF THAT RULE AND NOT TIDINESS. *** docs/decisions/0042.

NO BREAKDOWN, NO GROUPING, NO `by_status` MAP, NO PER-ORGANIZATION FIGURE. Every one of those transposes into a MAPPING, and the mapping is the object docs/decisions/0028 Decision 1 refuses. A count is one number; the moment it is keyed by anything it stops being a count and becomes a table.

*** THIS DOES NOT CONTRADICT platform.organizations.list's 'IT RETURNS NO COUNTS' — READ THEM TOGETHER. *** That sentence refuses a COUNT COLUMN ON A ROW: 'how many customers does this Organization have', which is a per-Organization figure over TENANT data behind whereWithTenant, and it is the transpose above. THIS is a single control-plane total over the Organization table itself, reads nothing behind whereWithTenant, and names no Organization. Different object, different population, and the sentence that refuses the first is the reason this one must stay scalar.

WHY IT NEEDS NO NEW PERMISSION, and the test is security.md §2a: a count is safe exactly when its consumer already holds enumeration over the counted population. `core.organization.list` holders enumerate Organizations deliberately, at `sensitive`, so this discloses nothing they cannot obtain by walking pages — more slowly, and at an audit row per page.

SHAPED THE SAME AS `urn:dudo:schema:template:1#/$defs/templateCountOutput` AND DELIBERATELY NOT SHARED WITH IT. They are the same shape by coincidence rather than by rule: different populations, different permissions, different sensitivity rungs. A shared def would couple two responses so that a legitimate addition to one — an `as_of` on this one, say — silently appeared on the other, which is the harmonising-two-rules-that-look-alike mistake. The duplication is two independent enforcement points of one rule, and the rule lives in 0042 rather than in either copy.

whoamiOutput.description: The calling operator's own context. IT HAS NO FIELD NAMING ANOTHER PRINCIPAL, and none may be added: the safety argument for this route is in its signature, not in a check.

permissions.description: THE REACHABLE PERMISSION SET, NOT THE HELD ONE — the intersection of what the platform role grants and what a route in this class can actually reach. For platform-admin today that is SIX, not the eight the role holds: core.principal.grant-platform-scope and core.marketplace.moderate are omitted because NO ROUTE EXISTS FOR EITHER, deliberately in the first case (no route creates a platform operator) and by phase in the second. Reporting them would describe a capability that does not exist and would have a console draw a button whose only outcome is a 404. It is the same ceiling-versus-floor intersection authorizer.ts computes, with the class's route table as the second bound. ADDING A ROUTE CHANGES THIS RESPONSE WITHOUT ANY ROLE CHANGING, so a client must not cache it across deployments or infer a role from it. UI HIDING IS PRESENTATION, NEVER SECURITY (0007 D8): every permission here is enforced again by Core on the call itself, and a console that ignored this list entirely would be ugly and exactly as safe.
